text: Program Description Economics is often emphasis on the teaching of theoretical knowledge than international trade or other courses. Main Courses and credits Each student must complete 54 credits of courses including 36 compulsory, 18 elective and 8 for a practicum requirement. More majors will be offered as enrollment expands such as Accounting and East Asian Studies (jointly offered with Nagoya University and Soongsil University) Compulsory Courses Credits Elective Courses Credits Accounting 3 Selected Topics in WTO and China 2 Intermediate Microeconomics 3 Chinese Economy 2 Intermediate Macroeconomics 3 Corporate Finance 3 Statistical Methods in Economics and Business 3 Investment Analysis 3 Legal Studies 3 Principles of Marketing 3 Econometrics 3 Chinese Business Law 2 Research Seminars 2 Applied Econometrics 3 Economics Research 3 Advanced International Trade Theory and Policy 3 History of Economic Thoughts 2 Financial Markets 3 Money and Banking 3 Principles of Management 2 Transnational Management 2 International Transportation and Logistics 3 Students may opt for one of the following two tracks or choose an individualized approach to complete 8 credits of courses across the tracks suggested below: Track 1 Track 2 Advanced Microeconomics 4 Applied International Economics 3 Advanced Macroeconomics 4 Applied Industrial Organization 3 Applied Public Finance 2 Internship and Career Development UIBE has special apartment to help international student find internship and employ chances in good companies and organizations. Thesis In the fourth year of their study, students must complete a thesis related to their major to meet the graduation requirements. The length of the thesis should be around 8000 words. The thesis is a milestone assessment on the intended level of achievement both in the major and the general learning outcomes by the students. Specifically, students, must demonstrate the ability to apply their learning to complex, unscripted problems in the context of their advanced studies, the mastery of the skills required for their disciplines as well as essential learning outcomes including the breadth and the depth of their knowledge, critical and creative thinking, problem solving, the ability to integrate knowledge and skills and present their work in an appropriate manner. Diploma Awarded Bachelor of Economics Academic Semesters There are 3 semesters in one academic year: fall, spring and summer. Fall and spring semesters consist of 14 weeks of normal classes and a summer term consists of 8 weeks of classes (except Practicum and Internship). Fall Semester: the beginning of September to next January Spring Semester: the beginning of March to the beginning of July Summer Vacation: the beginning of July to the end of August Time Registration Time of Spring Semester: February 27-March 2 Beginning Time of Spring Semester: March 5 Note: The course requires students to pay the tuition or admission deposit before issuing the admission package.
